definitions.type: operator on a metric space X, a positive real s, a positive real δ and a subset A⊆X, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For a metric space X, s>0, δ>0 and A⊆X, Hscale(s,δ,A)=inf{Σ_{i≥0}(diam U_i)^s : A⊆⋃_{i≥0}U_i and diam U_i≤δ for every i}. Covers are countable (finite covers are padded by empty sets). The diameter is the supremum of pairwise distances, with diameter of the empty set zero and unbounded diameter +∞; an empty member contributes zero. Sums, infima and suprema are in [0,∞], with inf ∅=∞. Covers are not required to be measurable.

definitions.type: operator on positive real exponents and subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For s>0 and a subset A of a metric space X, Hmeasure(s,A)=sup_{δ>0}Hscale(s,δ,A). This is precisely the unnormalized Hausdorff measure convention in problem.md:34-42.

definitions.type: operator on subsets of metric spaces, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: For A⊆X, hdim(A)=sup{a∈[0,∞):Hnative(a,A)=∞}, with the empty supremum equal to zero and real exponents embedded into [0,∞]. This is the native dimH definition (the exponent is represented by a nonnegative real). It is the usual Hausdorff dimension; in particular the definition assigns zero to the empty set.

definitions.type: operator on a real exponent a and a subset A of an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure, valued in [0,∞]
definitions.definition: Hnative(a,A) denotes the native value (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a)(A) on X. Its full covering formula is sup_{r∈(0,∞]} inf_{T:ℕ→Set X, A⊆⋃_i T_i, ∀i ediam(T_i)≤r} Σ_i w_a(T_i), where w_a(T)=0 for T empty and w_a(T)=(ediam T)^a otherwise; all diameters and operations here are extended nonnegative real operations, including extended real powers. Thus empty sets are zero even at exponent zero. The native definition is the Borel measure Measure.mkMetric(r↦r^a). For ordinary metric spaces ediam is the extended-valued supremum of ordinary distances.

inputs.statement: For every extended metric space X with a measurable space structure equal to its Borel structure, every real a and every A⊆X, Hnative(a,A)=sup_{r∈[0,∞], r>0} inf_{T:ℕ→Set X, A⊆⋃_i T_i, ∀i ediam(T_i)≤r} Σ_i sup_{h:T_i.Nonempty}(ediam(T_i))^a. The inner supremum is zero for an empty T_i and is the indicated power otherwise.

output.statement: For every metric space X, every A⊆X and every real s>0, Hmeasure(s,A)=Hnative(s,A). Moreover Hmeasure(s,A)=0 if hdim(A)<s; Hmeasure(s,A)=∞ if s<hdim(A); Hmeasure(s,A)=0 implies hdim(A)≤s; and Hmeasure(s,A)=∞ implies s≤hdim(A).

argument.text: Fix a metric space X, a subset A⊆X and s>0. Regard its metric as an extended metric and give X its Borel measurable structure. M001 gives the native covering formula. At every finite positive scale its inner infimum is exactly Hscale(s,δ,A): extended diameter agrees with ordinary diameter on bounded sets, nonempty-member costs agree, and both conventions make empty members zero. Infinite-diameter sets cannot occur at a finite scale. The extra scale r=∞ in M001 contributes no more than any finite-scale infimum because its cover class is larger. Thus its inclusion does not change the supremum over finite positive scales. Hence Hnative(s,A)=Hmeasure(s,A).

produces.statement: For the arbitrary X,A and s>0, Hnative(s,A)=Hmeasure(s,A).

argument.text: Using F001, apply M002 in the case s<hdim(A) to obtain Hmeasure(s,A)=∞. Apply M003 in the case hdim(A)<s to obtain Hmeasure(s,A)=0. If Hmeasure(s,A)=0, F001 makes Hnative(s,A)=0≠∞, so M004 gives hdim(A)≤s. If Hmeasure(s,A)=∞, then F001 and the supremum definition of hdim show s≤hdim(A), since s is one of its nonnegative exponents with infinite native measure. Each implication is conditional only on its displayed antecedent and is closed here; X,A,s were arbitrary. This proves every asserted clause.
